title: Discourse on Faith
subtitle: From the Catechetical Discourses, opening sections
source: Early 20th-century English translations of Symeon's Catechetical Discourses are in the public domain.

sections.title: Hear Me, Brothers
paragraphs: Brothers and fathers, hear me as I tell you of a great wonder. Hear, and do not lose heart, for I am about to speak of grace, and grace is given to those who ask. The Lord said: Knock, and it shall be opened to you. To us also, this very day, the door is opened, if we will but knock with faith.

I do not speak from books alone, nor from the words of others. I speak of what God Himself has done in me, the least of His servants, that you may know He is the same God yesterday, today, and forever, and that the gifts He gave to His apostles He gives even now to those who love Him.
notes: Symeon insists on personal experience of grace, against contemporaries who said the apostolic charisms had ceased. This insistence shaped Eastern hesychasm for the next thousand years.

sections.title: The Light That Was Seen
paragraphs: When I was yet a young man living in the world, the grace of God came upon me one night as I prayed, and a divine light suddenly shone in the room. The room was filled with light, and I no longer knew whether I was in the body or out of the body. I saw nothing but light, and within the light I saw Him whom my soul loved.

Afterwards the light departed, and I found myself weeping for joy and wonder, and longing for nothing else but that the light should come again. From that day I sought it always, and the Lord who is faithful did not refuse it to His servant.
notes: Symeon's vision of the uncreated light is the central event of his theology. The hesychast fathers, especially Gregory Palamas three centuries later, drew heavily on these accounts.

sections.title: On Tears and Repentance
paragraphs: He who has not learned to weep for his sins has not yet begun the Christian life. Tears are the second baptism, washing the soul of all that has clung to it since the first.

Do not despise the gift of tears, nor force them when they do not come. Pray, fast, keep watch over your heart, and the gift will be given when God sees that you are ready. And when it is given, do not boast of it, for the moment you boast it will leave you.
